name: Two state variables: energy reserves and gut contents (illustrative)
description: Demonstrates a model with two named state variables and expressions that depend on state and time. Energy reserves x are lethal at 0; gut contents g are not lethal at 0 (an empty gut is allowed). Each period the animal chooses to forage or rest. Foraging finds food with a probability that declines as the gut fills (satiation) and carries a predation risk that is higher for lean animals (which forage less carefully) and rises late in the season. Digestion moves 1 unit from gut to reserves each period; resting costs 1 unit of reserves. Terminal fitness increases with reserves. This example is illustrative only: its parameters are not taken from a published study.
